column1: Where can you get official PDF approach plates and IFR charts (high and low)?
column2: FAA.gov; printed NGA High Approach Playbook East also used; SkyVector/ForeFlight ultimately pull from these sources.

column1: What does the Trouble T on an approach plate header indicate?
column2: Takeoff issues / complications out of that airport (often lighting-related notes).

column1: What does a dot above an ALS code (e.g. A5) mean?
column2: Sequence flashers / strobe lights associated with that approach lighting system.

column1: MSA vs Emergency Safe Altitude — radius and clearance?
column2: MSA typically based on a ~25 NM circle about the defining navaid (quadrants). ESA out to 100 NM: 1000 ft obstacle clearance in flat terrain, 2000 ft in designated mountainous terrain.

column1: CNAF 3710 single-pilot RVR floor vs a plate showing 18 RVR (Atlantic City ILS example)?
column2: 3710 requires no lower than ~24 RVR (½ mile); 18 RVR on the civil plate is not enough for single-pilot rules.

column1: If MALSR is OTS on an ILS that was designed for 1800 RVR, what correction is typical?
column2: Increase RVR to 4000 (~¾ mile) per inoperative-components table / plate note (verify plate-specific notes).

column1: What is a displaced threshold usable for, and not usable for?
column2: Usable for takeoff roll and landing rollout; not a legal touchdown point (pavement not hardened for landings).

column1: Are T-45s authorized for land-and-hold-short (LAHSO) operations?
column2: No — T-45s are not really authorized for LAHSO.

column1: If a low approach plate omits Emergency Safe Altitude, what chart altitude can substitute conceptually?
column2: OROCA (off-route obstruction clearance altitude) — same 1000/2000 ft clearance idea.

column1: How is pilot-controlled lighting depicted on plates?
column2: Lighting symbology as a black circle with white lettering; click frequency to raise/lower intensity.

column1: At the outer marker on an ILS, centered glide slope should show what?
column2: The published glide-slope altitude at that fix (e.g. 1433 MSL at Tuscaloosa example). Mismatch → consider localizer-only and time from FAF.

column1: Approx VSI for a 3° glide path at 120 kt ground speed (descent gradient table)?
For PAR minima under single-pilot 3710 rules, what adjustment is emphasized?
column2: Add 100 ft to height-above-touchdown (and correspondingly to DA) so HAT is at least ~200 ft.

column1: Frequency order typically listed on the plate header?
column2: ATIS, Approach Control, Tower, Ground, Clearance Delivery (plus ASR/PAR note if applicable).
